name: peano_arithmetic
note_on_induction_vs_specification: synth2_induce_chain's own clause-search template is fixed to a UNARY target with one binary chain predicate (target(X):-chain(X,Y),target(Y)) -- it cannot SEARCH for a 3-argument relation like plus(A,B,C). These rules are the classic, well-known Peano encoding, HAND-SPECIFIED (not induced by the search engine), but VERIFIED the same rigorous way as every induced result in this registry: real execution, held-back blind checks at values never exercised during the visible proof, and (novel here) a full consistency SWEEP against native arithmetic.

rules.pred1_chain: rule pred1("v:N", "v:N-1").  -- enumerated successor/predecessor facts, one per adjacent pair
rules.plus:
rule plus(A, "v:0", A).
rule plus(A, B, C) :- pred1(B, B2), pred1(C, C2), plus(A, B2, C2).
rules.sum1n:
rule sum1n("v:0", "v:0").
rule sum1n(N, Total) :- pred1(N, N2), sum1n(N2, PrevTotal), plus(PrevTotal, N, Total).

provenance: directly requested: user noted sum_1_to_n implicitly needs a loop, that a proven step-down-by-2 (pred2, used for is_even) implies step-down-by-1 (pred1) should also work, and that a 'numerically controlled loop' should become a callable, registered building block -- confirmed pred1 generalizes identically to pred2 first, then built plus/sum1n on top of it exactly as Peano arithmetic constructs addition from succession and summation from addition.

consistency_sweep_vs_native_arithmetic.description: user: 'we *should* be able to find a way to relate those sorts of operations to the standard arithmetic operations, I think...' -- swept ALL (A,B) pairs for A,B in 0..8 (81 total), comparing plus(A,B,native_A_plus_B) against PatLang's own real + operator

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_while_building: first draft used a fake, undefined 'true(A)' predicate as the plus base case's body (rule plus(A,"v:0",A):-true(A).) -- nothing satisfies an undefined predicate, so the base case could never fire at all. Confirmed the correct form (a bodiless rule with a repeated head variable, rule plus(A,"v:0",A).) is valid syntax via a direct isolated test BEFORE using it, rather than guessing.

sum1n(10,55) initially failed (0 solutions) because the pred1 background facts only covered 1..20, but plus's own recursion needs pred1 facts covering intermediate values up to the TOTAL (55), not just up to N -- a real range-sizing bug in the test setup, fixed by extending the range to 60.
